title: body-fitted tet10 linear-elastic reference FEA (engine.verify.reference_fea_tet)

governing_equations.name: linear static equilibrium
governing_equations.description: Assembled quadratic tetrahedral (tet10) stiffness K times nodal displacement u equals nodal load F; solved by SuperLU direct (below the DOF cap) or Jacobi-preconditioned CG above it.

governing_equations.name: isotropic linear elasticity
governing_equations.expr: sigma = D(E, nu) : epsilon,  epsilon = sym(grad u)
governing_equations.description: Small-strain constitutive law; von Mises reduces the stress tensor to the reported scalar.

governing_equations.name: nodal stress recovery
governing_equations.expr: sigma_node = mean over incident elements of ( D B(x_node) u_e )
governing_equations.description: Stress is evaluated at each element's 10 nodes (not the element average) and averaged across elements meeting each node, so a surface peak is not smeared into the interior. This recovered surface peak converges to the true concentration under refinement.

assumptions: Linear elastic, small displacement, small strain — no plasticity, contact, or geometric nonlinearity.

Quadratic C0 tetrahedral (tet10) elements on a gmsh body-fitted conforming mesh; curved boundaries are meshed as true surfaces, NOT occupancy-sampled — this is the qualitative difference from the hex8/voxel path (ace_fea).
Geometry must be a gmsh-meshable watertight solid (an OCC primitive/fillet, or a watertight surface STL from the kernel tessellator).
A point load's resultant is spread equally over the selected surface nodes (same convention as the hex8 path).

boundary_conditions.fixtures: clamped = all 3 translational DOF fixed on selected nodes; pinned constrains the named dof_constrained subset. Selectors resolve to mesh nodes via a geometric plane/box test on mm coordinates.
boundary_conditions.loads: point = resultant N distributed equally over the selected surface nodes along the given direction. Body/pressure loads are not yet supported by the tet path.
boundary_conditions.selector_count_unit: nodes (mesh nodes satisfying the geometric selector)

discretization.notes: gmsh OCC/STL body-fitted conforming mesh at elem_size_mm; ElementOrder=2 with HighOrderOptimize to untangle curved elements. Fillet element size drives convergence of the recovered surface peak.

validation.ground_truth: Peterson/Pilkey stepped-bar shoulder-fillet-in-tension Kt = 1.667 for d=16, D=24, r=2.4 mm (D/d=1.5, r/d=0.15, h/r=1.667); sigma_nom = P/(pi d^2/4). Source: Pilkey, Peterson's Stress Concentration Factors, chart 3.4.

error_band.far_field_nominal: within 2% of P/A at every size

validation.direction: under-predicts the fillet Kt and CONVERGES from below (monotone up 1.545 -> 1.610 -> 1.652) toward 1.667 with no overshoot — the qualitatively-correct convergence the voxel hex8 path (ace_fea) never achieves (it scatters -6%..+44%, non-convergent).

caveats: Surface stress is nodal-averaged recovery, NOT full superconvergent patch recovery (SPR) — good enough to converge from below, but the finest-mesh peak is still a few percent shy of the analytic Kt.
Robustness is bounded by gmsh: the geometry must be a watertight, gmsh-meshable solid; a non-watertight STL fails loudly at the surface-loop-to-volume step rather than producing garbage.
The Kt pin ladder stops at elem_size ~ r/2.4 (1.0 mm) for runtime (~1.5 min total); finer meshes would tighten the residual but are not pinned here.
Point/clamped BCs only; body and pressure loads are not yet implemented in the tet path.

limits_of_validity.regime: linear elastic, deflection << member size, gmsh-meshable watertight geometry
limits_of_validity.resolution: fillet peak trustworthy to a few percent at elem_size <= r/2.4; coarser meshes under-read the peak (converging from below)
limits_of_validity.recovery: nodal-averaged surface stress; not SPR — treat the last-digit of a reported peak as approximate
